punchline: Rosling replaced rich-versus-poor with four income levels, and the biggest groups turned out to be in the middle two.
thirty_sec: Hans Rosling's gap instinct is the urge to split the world into rich and poor. He offers four income levels instead: under $2 a day, about 1 billion people; $2 to $8, about 3 billion; $8 to $32, about 2 billion; and over $32, about 1 billion. That puts roughly five of seven billion in the two middle levels. He sets it out in Factfulness.
